verdicts.note: 'POST-MARITAL RESIDENCE PATTERNS AND THE TIMING OF REPRODUCTION' in a MATRILINEAL Tibetan population, and it states the chapter's own conditionality: the relationship depends on whether CO-RESIDENT KIN ARE COOPERATORS OR COMPETITORS. That is §5's two-sign problem, derived from theory rather than observed as a nuisance. Priority read.
Parental awareness of child abuse.
Protective factors against partner violence among married adolescents in Bangladesh.
Personal essay on pregnancy in surgical residency.
Parental burnout in Togo.
No abstract; 'Happiness in Old Age: The Daughter Connection'.
Mothers CO-RESIDING WITH EXTENDED KIN during partnership transitions, treating kin co-residence as a response to relationship change. Threat 2 again: the family event drives the arrangement.
Remote work and work-life balance during COVID.

IDENTIFIED, AND A DESIGN §4 NEVER ENUMERATED. 'Dreaming of leaving the nest? IMMIGRATION STATUS and the living arrangements of DACAmented' uses DACA ELIGIBILITY CUTOFFS in an event study with difference-in-differences to estimate effects on LIVING ARRANGEMENTS. A legal-status discontinuity acting directly on whether young adults leave the parental home -- design 6's shape, from immigration law rather than benefit law. Priority read, and it should be added to §4's enumeration.
No abstract; family size, labour supply and job prestige across Chinese censuses.

Whether GRANDPARENTAL CHILDCARE raises the likelihood and speed of transition to SECOND BIRTH in China. C.2.a's exposure with a parity-specific fertility outcome; at least the fourth near-identical China second-birth childcare record in this frame, which is itself worth reporting.
Children's indirect exposure to the justice system through parents or CORESIDENT ADULTS.
The developmental cycle of the domestic group, with the COURTSHIP PHASE as its first stage. The classic anthropological framing of the household as a phase-structured object rather than a state.
Children's DELAYED AND UNSTABLE transitions to adulthood against midlife parents' depressive symptoms and daily living. The parents'-side outcome, now the sixth such record.

Published ESR version of the reclassified anchor: regular GRANDPARENTAL CHILDCARE and the second-birth transition, framed through the work-family incompatibility that leaves fertility desires unrealised. C.2.a's.
Young people's preference for secure employment as they progress through the transition to adulthood.
Pension policy in ageing emerging Asian economies.
Young children's LIVING ARRANGEMENT and migrant parents' sleep health in South Africa. The arrangement is between parent and young child.
Transformation of family structure in SOUTHEAST ASIA under fertility decline, migration and longer lives. Regional exposure trend; the reverse arrow is in the framing.
Family helpers of Chinese women entrepreneurs.
Neolithic pedigrees reconstructing kinship and residence from ancient DNA. The residence rule inferred archaeologically; no fertility estimate.

The role of CO-RESIDENCE and household composition in Indian women's labour force participation and domestic work. Arrangement as exposure, labour as outcome -- the route-out the scope predicted would be largest, in a fifth setting.

THE HAND-ADDED RECORD, now with an abstract. LIVING ARRANGEMENTS and HOMEOWNERSHIP against FERTILITY INTENTION in Indonesia, ordinal logistic regression on national survey data. It carries both Wall 1 variables in one model, and it is one of the two records the boolean query could not reach -- the 226 supplement has now earned itself back twice.

Households, women's roles and prestige as determinants of nuptiality and FERTILITY differentials in MALI, with residential units as the analytic unit and a point beyond which household size reduces members' income. An arrangement-to-fertility argument in a sub-Saharan pastoral setting the frame otherwise misses entirely.
Adulthood milestones and paternity after childhood cancer.

Grandparental care against CHILDREN'S EFFORTS, China Family Panel Studies, using two instruments including the COMMUNITY CAREGIVING RATE. C.2.a's exposure and a child outcome, but the community-rate instrument is a strategy this chapter could borrow for co-residence.
No abstract; life-course perspective on young adults' working lives and mental health.
Companion review to the Latin American 'nini' study, noting that EARLY union formation and parenthood are pervasive in the region alongside disengagement.
Custody, CO-RESIDENCE and care of minor children among parents on probation.
Personal essay by an oncologist on becoming a father.
No abstract; 'Culture and the family' in the Handbook of the Economics of the Family. D.1.a/D.2.b's.

'CORESIDING WITH PARENTS, son preference, and WOMEN'S DESIRE FOR ADDITIONAL CHILDREN IN VIETNAM' -- co-residence in the exposure and a fertility-desire outcome, with the in-laws' pressure for a male heir as the stated mechanism, set against declining multigenerational households under urbanisation. Directly on the extended arm's estimand.
Dutch translation of a parental stress scale.

'THE TRIFECTA OF ADULTHOOD: HOUSING, PARTNERING AND CHILDBEARING TRAJECTORIES', on the de-standardisation of adulthood pathways in EAST ASIA. All three of Wall 1's elements taken as one trajectory object, in the region where the extended configuration dominates. The best single framing of the chapter's whole problem found in the screen.
Japanese women caring simultaneously for children and older parents.

Panel study of Indian adolescent girls who MOVE TO MARITAL HOUSEHOLDS, OFTEN CO-RESIDING WITH IN-LAWS, and begin childbearing. The arrangement and the birth arrive together by construction -- §3's sequence problem in its starkest form -- but the estimated outcome is empowerment.
Case-based essay on social prescribing in perinatal mental health.
No abstract; family structure type and household energy consumption in China.

Qualitative accounts of marriage and fertility in Bali, where PATRILOCAL (purusa) marriage and patrilineal inheritance make a son the family successor. The residence rule and the fertility consequence in one account; qualitative.
Bronze Age Korean dwelling EXTENSION and its socioeconomic significance -- household growth read off house floor area. Archaeological.

Experiments with women in MATRILOCAL AND PATRILOCAL communities in rural Malawi, showing the competitiveness gender gap varies by residence system. The residence rule as an experimental stratifier; outcome is competitiveness.
Step-grandparental investment by whether the step-grandparent CO-RESIDED with the grandchild's parent in childhood. Co-residence as a historical exposure, investment as outcome.
Young adults living with home mechanical ventilation.
Human-bird relations in Norwegian fiction.
Letter on mentorship and motherhood in residency.

DELAYED TRANSITION TO ADULTHOOD in SPAIN and the intergenerational transmission of disadvantage, using an intersectional quantitative framework. The registered setting, with inequality as the organising variable rather than culture.
Family dynamics after a gay son comes out in Hong Kong.
Molecular dynamics of sperm-egg complexation. The fertilization homonym.
Grandparents, domestic workers and preschools as simultaneous childcare sources against maternal employment in Hong Kong. C.2.a's, with the paid-substitute point again.

'WHY DO YOUNG ADULTS CORESIDE WITH THEIR PARENTS?' in Real Estate Economics: nearly one in two US adults aged 18-29 now lives with parents against one in four in 1960, and a Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition identifies a role for HOUSING AFFORDABILITY against the labour-market and marriage-delay explanations. It decomposes the very trend the pre-launch arm rests on, and it puts Wall 1's variable in competition with the alternatives rather than assuming one. Second-read packet.
Labour immobility and its efficiency costs in Britain.
No abstract; co-determinants of co-residence among older persons in India.
No abstract; a voluntary hosting programme for child-welfare families.
Reproductive coercion in sub-Saharan settings.
Opinion piece on filial piety and migrant peasant families in China; duplicate of an earlier record.
